Eight types of day, and who has them

day_types.Rd

A summary of the eight day types found by grouping the 2025 ATUS diary days with survey-weighted k-means clustering on the 15 activity categories. All percentages are survey-weighted.

Usage

day_types

Format

A tibble with 8 rows and 12 columns:

day_type

Name of the day type.

tagline

One-line description.

n_respondents

Number of survey days of this type (unweighted).

share

Estimated percentage of all days of the year that are of this type.

pct_weekend

Percentage of these days that fall on a weekend.

mean_age

Average age of the people having this type of day.

pct_female

Percentage of these days had by women.

pct_employed

Percentage had by employed people.

pct_student

Percentage had by students.

pct_child_under_6

Percentage had by people whose youngest child in the household is under 6.

pct_aged_65_plus

Percentage had by people aged 65 and over.

match_cutoff

The same for every type: 95% of the real survey days are no more than this many hours apart from their closest type (see match_my_day()). Used to decide whether a match is close.

Source

Derived from atus_days. Prepared in data-raw/atus_days.R.

Details

Days vary continuously, so the types are useful summaries rather than sharp categories. vignette("dayalike") checks how well a day keeps its type when the time spent on each activity is slightly off.
